The decisive error was GameTheory_Expert's conclusion that guessing (2, 11, 17) guarantees all 30 coins ($30,000). That claim ignores that the boxes are shuffled, so Bob doesn't know which box holds which count. For example, if the counts are (12, 6, 18) and the 11-guess lands on the 6-coin box, Bob earns nothing from that box. The agent also treated "minimum winnings" as the best guaranteed outcome, when the question asks for the worst case over all placements. VerificationExpert then endorsed the flawed result at step 2 without testing it against permutations, but the original mistake was made at step 1.
